content: The provided text is a detailed pharmacological interaction guide, but it is presented in a fragmented and encoded format. 1. Darunavir and Pimozide: Darunavir significantly increases the plasma levels and effects of pimozide by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction is contraindicated due to the risk of QT prolongation and potential cardiac toxicity. 2. Cobicistat and Pimozide: Cobicistat also increases pimozide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This interaction is contraindicated for the same reasons as above. 3. Cobicistat and CYP2D6 Substrates: Cobicistat can increase pimozide levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 4. Darunavir and Pioglitazone: Darunavir may increase pioglitazone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but it is considered minor. 5. Cobicistat and Pirtobrutinib: Cobicistat increases pirtobrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the patient is on a 50 mg daily dose, discontinue pirtobrutinib during strong CYP3A inhibitor use. Resume the original dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 5 half-lives. 6. Darunavir and Pirtobrutinib: Darunavir also increases pirtobrutinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The same dose adjustment recommendations apply as with cobicistat. 7. Darunavir and Pitavastatin: Darunavir increases pitavastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 8. Cobicistat and Pitavastatin: Cobicistat similarly increases pitavastatin levels. Start with the lowest recommended dose of pitavastatin and titrate while monitoring for safety. 9. Darunavir and Pitolisant: Darunavir increases pitolisant levels by inhibiting both CYP3A4 and CYP2D6. Reduce the pitolisant dose by half when initiating strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 10. Darunavir and Polatuzumab Vedotin: Darunavir increases polatuzumab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely, as polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to MMAE, a CYP3A4 substrate, which may increase toxicity. 11. Cobicistat and Polatuzumab Vedotin: Cobicistat also increases polatuzumab vedotin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The same precautions apply. 12. Darunavir and Pomalidomide: Darunavir increases pomalidomide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Darunavir and Ponatinib: Darunavir increases ponatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Cobicistat and Ponatinib: Cobicistat also increases ponatinib levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Posaconazole and Darunavir: Posaconazole increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Posaconazole and Cobicistat: Posaconazole increases cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Darunavir and Pralsetinib: Darunavir increases pralsetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Cobicistat and Pralsetinib: Cobicistat also increases pralsetinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 19. Darunavir and Pramlintide: Darunavir may reduce the effects of pramlintide due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Darunavir and Pravastatin: Darunavir increases pravastatin levels by an unknown mechanism and by inhibiting CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 21. Cobicistat and Pravastatin: Cobicistat increases pravastatin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. 22. Cobicistat and Praziquantel: Cobicistat increases praziquantel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Darunavir and Prednisolone: Darunavir increases prednisolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Darunavir and Prednisone: Darunavir increases prednisone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, while prednisone decreases darunavir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Darunavir and Primaquine: Darunavir increases primaquine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Primidone and Darunavir: Primidone decreases darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 27. Primidone and Cobicistat: Primidone decreases cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 induction. This interaction is contraindicated. 28. Darunavir and Progesterone (Intravaginal Gel): Darunavir increases progesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Cobicistat and Progesterone (Intravaginal Gel): Cobicistat also increases progesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Darunavir and Progesterone (Micronized): Darunavir increases micronized progesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Cobicistat and Progesterone (Micronized): Cobicistat increases micronized progesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 32. Darunavir and Progesterone (Natural): Darunavir increases natural progesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 33. Cobicistat and Progesterone (Natural): Cobicistat increases natural progesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 34. Cobicistat and Propafenone: Cobicistat increases propafenone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Darunavir and Propafenone: Darunavir increases propafenone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Cobicistat and Protriptyline: Cobicistat increases protriptyline levels. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect and monitor closely. 37. Cobicistat and Quazepam: Cobicistat increases quazepam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 38. Darunavir and Quazepam: Darunavir increases quazepam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 39. Darunavir and Quetiapine: Darunavir increases quetiapine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the quetiapine dose to one-sixth of the current dose and monitor for adverse reactions. 40. Cobicistat and Quetiapine: Cobicistat increases quetiapine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 41. Darunavir and Quinidine: Darunavir increases quinidine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 42. Cobicistat and Quinidine: Cobicistat increases quinidine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Cobicistat and Quinine: Cobicistat increases quinine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 44. Darunavir and Quinine: Darunavir increases quinine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 45. Quinupristin/Dalfopristin and Darunavir: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Cobicistat and Quizartinib: Cobicistat increases quizartinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 47. Darunavir and Quizartinib: Darunavir increases quizartinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 48. Cobicistat and Rabeprazole: Cobicistat increases rabeprazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 49. Darunavir and Rabeprazole: Darunavir increases rabeprazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 50. Darunavir and Ramelteon: Darunavir increases ramelteon levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 51. Darunavir and Ranolazine: Darunavir increases ranolazine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This interaction is contraindicated. 52. Cobicistat and Ranolazine: Cobicistat increases ranolazine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This interaction is contraindicated. 53. Darunavir and Red Yeast Rice: Darunavir increases red yeast rice levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 54. Darunavir and Regorafenib: Darunavir increases regorafenib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This interaction is contraindicated. 55. Darunavir and Repaglinide: Darunavir increases repaglinide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Cobicistat and Repaglinide: Cobicistat increases repaglinide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Darunavir and Repotrectinib: Darunavir increases repotrectinib levels via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 58. Cobicistat and Repotrectinib: Cobicistat increases repotrectinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 59. Cobicistat and Resmetirom: Cobicistat increases resmetirom levels. Avoid coadministration with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. 60. Cobicistat and Ribociclib: Cobicistat increases ribociclib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 61. Darunavir and Ribociclib: Darunavir increases ribociclib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 62. Rifabutin and Cobicistat: Rifabutin decreases cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 induction. Reduce the rifabutin dose to 150 mg every other day and monitor for neutropenia and uveitis. 63. Rifabutin and Darunavir: Rifabutin decreases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 64. Rifampin and Darunavir: Rifampin decreases darunavir levels by increasing metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 65. Rifampin and Cobicistat: Rifampin decreases cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 induction. This interaction is contraindicated. 66. Rifapentine and Darunavir: Rifapentine decreases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely.
